topic: data retention in an analytics warehouse
old_rule: Every raw event table keeps 400 days of data, and once a month the retention steward opens a purge ticket listing older partitions, the table owners approve it, and the steward runs the monthly purge.
new_rule: Every raw event table carries a 180-day partition expiry in its table definition, and a nightly expiry job drops expired partitions automatically with no approval step.

planted.text: No retention steward reviews the list of expired partitions before the nightly job drops them.
An expired partition is dropped without anyone having to approve it first.
Raw tables no longer reach back a full year, so year-over-year queries against them will come back short.
Expiry is a property of the table itself, not something each analyst decides when writing a query.
Each night's rollup partition is computed from the raw partition of the day before rather than fed by a separate streaming pipeline.
This warehouse keeps no such copy, so a dropped partition cannot be restored by anyone.
planted.licence: Some warehouses copy expired partitions to cold storage before dropping them.
